jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer
jobs.jobDescription: Own the ledger and payment-routing services. Requirements: 5+ years of backend experience, strong Postgres skills, experience designing idempotent APIs, event-driven systems on Kafka, and operating services with on-call responsibility. Nice to have: Go, experience with caching layers such as Redis.
jobs.notes: Recruiter said the loop is phone screen, system design, then a behavioral round with the hiring manager. Team is 8 engineers.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, Patient Platform
jobs.jobDescription: Build APIs for scheduling and patient records. Requirements: Python or Node, REST design, relational modelling, HIPAA awareness, and clear communication with clinical product partners. You will mentor junior engineers.
jobs.notes: Referral from a former colleague. Interview is heavy on API design and past project stories.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.jobDescription: Lead design of the shipment-tracking platform handling 40M events/day. Requirements: distributed systems, caching and data-partitioning strategies, capacity planning, and technical leadership across teams.
jobs.notes: Onsite is 4 rounds: coding, system design, architecture deep dive, leadership.

jobs.title: Full Stack Engineer
jobs.jobDescription: Work on the creator dashboard (React, TypeScript, Node). Requirements: component design, performance profiling, GraphQL, and comfort shipping in small, fast iterations with designers.
jobs.notes: Take-home first, then a pairing session and a culture round.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.jobDescription: Build internal developer tooling on AWS. Requirements: Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, observability, and Postgres operations. Experience with CDN and edge caching is a plus.
jobs.notes: Phone screen with a recruiter, then a technical round on infrastructure and incident handling.

jobs.title: Software Engineer II
jobs.jobDescription: Modernise internal lending tools. Requirements: Java or Kotlin, SQL performance tuning, secure coding, and working with compliance reviewers. Strong collaboration and stakeholder skills expected.
jobs.notes: Panel interview with two engineers and a product owner.

notes.title: Northwind phone screen
notes.content: Spoke with the hiring manager for 30 minutes. Walked through my last role owning a payments webhook service. Asked about idempotency keys and how I handle duplicate events from Kafka. I answered well on idempotency but rambled when asked why I left my last team. Follow-up: tighten my career story to two minutes.

notes.title: Northwind system design: payment status API
notes.content: Designed a payment status lookup API with 20k reads per second. I proposed a Redis cache in front of Postgres but could not explain the invalidation strategy when a payment changes state. The interviewer asked about write-through versus cache-aside and stale reads for a ledger. I hesitated and said 'we could just set a short TTL'. Clear weak spot: caching trade-offs and consistency.

notes.title: Northwind behavioral round
notes.content: Questions about conflict with a teammate and a project that missed its deadline. I described the situation but skipped the result and what I learned, so the answers felt incomplete. The manager hinted that she wanted a clear structure. I should practise STAR answers with measurable outcomes.

notes.title: Northwind Postgres follow-up questions
notes.content: Short technical chat on indexing: composite index column order, partial indexes for active payments, and why a sequential scan can beat an index. Felt confident. Used EXPLAIN ANALYZE examples from my own projects.

notes.title: Northwind debrief with recruiter
notes.content: Recruiter feedback: strong on Postgres and Kafka, wants deeper reasoning about cache invalidation and more structured storytelling in behavioral answers. No offer yet, decision expected next week.

notes.title: Lumen recruiter screen
notes.content: Covered salary range, remote policy, and why healthcare. Recruiter stressed that clinical partners need plain-language explanations. I gave a vague answer about why I want to work in healthcare and had no concrete story ready.

notes.title: Lumen API design exercise
notes.content: Designed REST endpoints for appointment scheduling including double-booking prevention with optimistic locking. Discussed pagination, versioning and audit logs for HIPAA. Good discussion; the interviewer liked the audit log idea. Slight stumble on rate limiting.

notes.title: Lumen behavioral with engineering manager
notes.content: Asked how I mentor junior engineers and about a time I disagreed with a product decision. My mentoring example was a rambling story without a clear result. I need a tighter situation-task-action-result structure and one example with numbers, like reduced review time by 30 percent.

notes.title: Lumen follow-up: performance question
notes.content: They asked how I would speed up a slow patient search endpoint. I jumped to caching the search results and was asked about stale patient data and cache invalidation when a record is updated. Again I could not explain the trade-offs between freshness and speed for sensitive data.

notes.title: Orbital coding round
notes.content: Implemented a sliding window rate limiter and an LRU cache. Passed all tests, discussed time complexity of both. Good round. Used a doubly linked list plus hash map for the LRU cache.

notes.title: Orbital system design: tracking events pipeline
notes.content: Whiteboarded ingestion of 40M events per day with Kafka, partitioning by shipment id, and a read model in Cassandra. Asked where a cache fits: I suggested caching the latest status per shipment but struggled with cache invalidation across regions and the cost of stale data. Caching trade-offs again. Partitioning and capacity maths went well.

notes.title: Orbital leadership round
notes.content: Questions on leading a migration across three teams and handling an underperforming engineer. I gave a strong story on the migration with outcomes but for the underperformer question I could not recall specifics and answered in generalities without STAR structure.

notes.title: Orbital architecture deep dive
notes.content: Deep dive into a past design of mine: event sourcing for order history. Defended the trade-offs of eventual consistency and replay costs. Asked about schema evolution of events; answered with versioned envelopes.

notes.title: Brightwave take-home review
notes.content: Built a small analytics dashboard in React with TypeScript. Feedback: clean components and good tests, but the list rendered slowly with 10k rows and I had not used virtualization or memoization. Performance profiling is a gap.

notes.title: Brightwave pairing session
notes.content: Paired on adding GraphQL pagination to the dashboard. Comfortable with Apollo hooks. Interviewer asked about HTTP caching and Apollo cache normalisation; I knew the basics but could not discuss when cached data becomes stale or how to evict it.

notes.title: Brightwave culture round
notes.content: Talked about working with designers and receiving critical feedback. My answer about handling feedback had no concrete example. The interviewer asked 'tell me about a time' twice and I stayed generic. Need prepared STAR stories for feedback and collaboration.

notes.title: Kestrel recruiter phone screen
notes.content: Discussed AWS experience, Terraform modules I maintain, and on-call load. Recruiter said the team values calm incident communication. No concerns raised.

notes.title: Kestrel infrastructure technical round
notes.content: Questions on Terraform state management, blue-green deploys, and CloudFront. When asked how to cache API responses at the CDN edge and purge them safely after a deploy, I only gave the TTL answer. Did not cover cache keys, stale-while-revalidate or purge strategy. Weak on caching trade-offs.

notes.title: Kestrel incident scenario
notes.content: Walked through a simulated database outage: triage, communication, rollback. Did well on technical steps. Asked for a real incident I led; I described it but without the timeline or measurable impact, so it was not a crisp STAR story.

notes.title: Meridian panel interview
notes.content: Two engineers and a product owner. Java collections, SQL window functions, and a question about working with compliance reviewers who block a release. My stakeholder example was vague on the actual outcome. Product owner wanted a specific story with a result.

notes.title: Meridian SQL tuning exercise
notes.content: Given a slow query joining loans and payments. Found a missing index and rewrote a correlated subquery as a join. Explained the query plan. Strong round.

notes.title: Meridian recruiter feedback
notes.content: Feedback: technically solid, but behavioral answers lacked structure and measurable results. Suggested using the STAR method.

notes.title: General: STAR method cheat sheet
notes.content: Reminder after several rounds: structure behavioral answers as Situation, Task, Action, Result. Always finish with a number or an outcome and one lesson. Keep each story under two minutes. Prepare five stories: conflict, failure, leadership, tight deadline, feedback.

notes.title: General: caching reading notes
notes.content: Notes to self on caching: cache-aside versus write-through versus write-behind, TTL versus explicit invalidation, cache stampede and request coalescing, stale-while-revalidate, and when stale data is acceptable (product catalog) versus not (balances, patient data). Practise explaining these with one example each.

notes.title: General: salary negotiation thoughts
notes.content: Ask for the range early, anchor with market data, and never give a number first if I can avoid it. Compare total compensation including equity and bonus rather than base salary alone.
